title: Shared fixture for spawning jit in CLI tests
description:
Give CLI integration tests one shared fixture that spawns `jit`, so no test file needs its own binary locator, repository setup, environment handling or id scraping.

## Background

No shared subprocess fixture exists. `fn jit_binary` is defined in 56 files under `crates/jit/tests/`; 43 files spawn through `assert_cmd`'s `cargo_bin!` and 69 through `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit")`. 56 files define a local `setup_test_repo` or `setup_repo`, and 33 more define differently named setups. 114 `split_whitespace` sites in 39 files parse human-readable output, most of them to scrape created ids. 20 test files and 8 source test modules hand-roll `git init`.

A few files remove chosen `JIT_*` variables (`steering_scenarios.rs`, `repo_discovery_tests.rs`, `profile_acceptance_tests.rs`, `project_config_tests.rs`, `failure_probe_fixture.rs`), but nothing removes them all. The product reads `JIT_AGENT_ID` at 10 sites, plus `JIT_DATA_DIR`, `JIT_WORKTREE_*`, `JIT_ALLOW_DELETION` and `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, so a developer's agent identity and data-directory overrides reach most spawned processes.

Shared test support (`crate::test_utils`, `crate::test_harness`, `crate::test_taxonomy`) is compiled once under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`, and every integration target enables that feature through the crate's self dev-dependency. `assert_cmd` is a dev-dependency, so library test support cannot name it. `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit` is set only while an integration target compiles.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Shared test support provides one CLI process fixture. It owns a temporary repository, which is uninitialised, initialised by `jit init`, or a repository from shared test support handed to it, and it removes the repository on drop.
- [hard] REQ-02: The fixture locates the `jit` binary built for the calling integration target through one shared construction path, so a test names no binary path, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit` or `cargo_bin!`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every process the fixture spawns starts with no inherited `JIT_*` variable. A test sets one only through the fixture, and the setting reaches that process alone.
- [hard] REQ-04: On request the fixture initialises git in its repository, with a fixed author identity and no dependency on the developer's global git configuration. It does so through a shared test-support function that in-process tests can also call.
- [hard] REQ-05: The fixture reads the ids of issues it creates from `--json` output.
- [hard] REQ-06: The environment scrub, git initialisation and id reading each have one owning test, and each of those tests passes alone and in parallel with the rest.

## Notes

The fixture hands tests a `std::process::Command` or a thin wrapper around one, so tests keep `assert_cmd`'s assertion traits from their own dev-dependency. It adds no integration target (`@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint`). `dev/TESTING.md` names it as the way to spawn `jit`.

planning.outcome: One shared test-support fixture spawns jit over a temporary repository it owns, with inherited JIT_* variables removed.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One new test-support module with its own unit tests; no consumer is migrated here.

title: Memory executor initialised through product initialisation
description:
Give in-process tests one memory executor that is set up by the product's own initialisation, so no test support restates configuration or index bytes.

## Background

Two memory executors exist. `crate::commands::test_helpers::memory_executor` seeds `[worktree] enforce_leases = "off"` and the data-root ignore file. `memory_executor` in `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/main.rs` seeds an empty configuration and a literal index body carrying `"schema_version": 2`, then delegates to the first. `TestHarness` (`crate::test_harness`) builds on the first.

Product initialisation exists only on `impl CommandExecutor<JsonFileStorage>` (`initialize_fresh_repository` and `run_initialization` in `crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs`), although both go through the generic `with_mutation_session`. `repository_state::initialize::structural_minimum_config` is the pure minimal configuration.

Users of the library executor: `commands/{batch_create,bulk_update,dependency,gate_check,gate,issue,mod,validate}.rs` and `test_harness.rs`. Users of the `fast_rules` copy: `fast_rules/{example_rulesets,label_query,label_strategic,validate_rule_runner,validation}_tests.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Product initialisation runs over any repository-state store, and the in-memory backend is initialised through the same code path as the JSON backend.
- [hard] REQ-02: `memory_executor` has one definition in shared test support. It seeds configuration and index by running product initialisation over the memory store, and no test support writes a literal schema version or index body.
- [hard] REQ-03: `fast_rules` defines no executor fixture, and `TestHarness` builds on the shared one.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test that relied on a fixture-specific configuration value declares that value itself and keeps the property it asserted.

title: cli_gate tests spawn jit through the shared process fixture
description:
Move the gate CLI tests in `crates/jit/tests/cli_gate` onto the shared CLI process fixture, so they carry no binary locator, repository setup or id scraping of their own.

## Background

Shared test support provides one CLI process fixture. It owns a temporary repository, spawns the `jit` binary built for the calling integration target with inherited `JIT_*` variables removed, initialises git on request and reads created ids from `--json` output. Before it existed, each CLI test file carried its own binary locator (`fn jit_binary`, `assert_cmd`'s `cargo_bin!` or `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit")`), its own repository setup (`setup_test_repo`, `setup_repo`, `setup`, `setup_test_env` and similar), private git helpers (`run_git`, `git`, `init_git`, `setup_git_repo`), and in places scraped ids from human-readable output with `split_whitespace`. Inherited `JIT_AGENT_ID`, `JIT_DATA_DIR`, `JIT_WORKTREE_*`, `JIT_ALLOW_DELETION` and `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` values leaked into those spawns.

`cli_gate` has 15 test files. 14 of them spawn through `cargo_bin!`, 11 define a local setup, and 8 parse human-readable output with `split_whitespace`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No file in this migration's scope defines or calls a binary locator, a repository setup or a git initialisation helper of its own; each test spawns `jit` through the shared CLI process fixture.
- [hard] REQ-02: No test in scope reads an id or other value from human-readable output; ids come from `--json` output.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test that depends on a `JIT_*` variable sets it through the fixture for the process it spawns.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each migrated test asserts the property it asserted before and passes alone, in any order and in parallel.

planning.outcome: The cli_gate suite spawns jit only through the shared CLI process fixture.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Mechanical replacement of local locators, setups and id scraping with one fixture across one integration target's files.

title: Server shutdown force-close test stays under the per-test bound
description:
Prove the drain entitlement at the shutdown-sequence layer with a short deadline, so no server test waits out the real five-second drain.

## Background

`crates/server/tests/server_integration/graceful_shutdown_tests.rs:538` (`test_jit_server_shutdown_force_closes_a_stalled_connection_and_exits_zero`) spawns `jit-server`, stalls a connection and waits the full `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (5 s, `crates/server/src/shutdown.rs:33`) before asserting the force-close. It took 5.32 s and is the last test to finish in the suite run.

`run_shutdown_sequence` (`shutdown.rs:152`) takes its drain deadline as a parameter and logs `drained_for_ms`. Its unit tests already pass a 300 ms deadline (`test_run_shutdown_sequence_force_closes_connections_that_outlive_the_deadline`, `:402`). A `test-support` build reads the serving process's deadline from `JIT_SERVER_DRAIN_DEADLINE_MS` (`configured_drain_deadline`). `test_the_drain_assertion_rejects_a_server_that_force_closes_early` (`:626`) uses that seam to show the drain assertion fails against a server that force-closes early.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A unit test of `run_shutdown_sequence` with a short deadline owns the entitlement: a stalled connection keeps running for at least the deadline before it is force-closed.
- [hard] REQ-02: The serving process enforces `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` when no test deadline is configured, proven without waiting for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: The process-level test proves the wiring with a short configured deadline: a stalled connection is force-closed, the process exits zero, and the log records completion. The drain assertion is still shown to fail against a server that force-closes early.
- [hard] REQ-04: No test in the server crate exceeds 5 s on a warm target at load ≤ 10.

planning.outcome: Drain entitlement is proven with a short deadline, and no server test waits the real five-second drain.
